Likely cause: restricted hip rotation
Lead hip turned 31° [4] at impact; ~45° is typical.
It may feel like you stay down, but at impact
your hips have moved toward the ball.
You set up well. On the way down your hips drift toward the ball, and by impact
they have moved 7% of your body height. My rule starts at 4%. Your chest then has to
stand up to make room for your arms. The likely reason is a lead hip that isn’t turning.
Read the full explanation
Backside touching a wall or golf bag. Slow half
swings, trail glute stays on the wall through
impact.
Both knees bent to 90°. Rotate slowly from
one side to the other, chest tall.
Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a
physiotherapist if you feel pain.

Why does it feel like I’m staying
down when I’m not?
The move happens below your eye line,
so you don’t see it. Your head stays
level, but by impact your hips have moved
7% of body height [3] toward the ball.
In the wall drill, the moment your trail
glute leaves the wall is that same move.
